definition: 2.0 means the improved version of something.
definition_2: We’ve made several improvements to create a better version of the original product.
example: Let's call this the Strategic Plan 2.0

definition: Looking at something in the broadest sense, consider the big picture of a situation or problem rather than getting hung up on the details.
definition_2: Let’s step back and look at the overall situation before discussing the smaller details.
example: Let’s take a 30,000-foot view on our customer acquisition strategy.

definition: Finding the way that will lead to the most progress with the least amount of work.
definition_2: Let’s focus on the few tasks that will create the biggest impact with the least effort.
example: We don't have time to do a full analysis.Let's 80/20 this.

definition: Something that has to get done.
definition_2: Please complete the updated report before tomorrow’s meeting.
example: Did any action items come out of the meeting?

definition: To make something actionable is to make it clear what someone needs to do and something that can be acted upon or turned into a concrete next step.
definition_2: The message should clearly explain what the recipient needs to do next.
example: Your email isn't actionable enough.What do you want the reader to do with your message?

definition: Information that can be acted upon or insights that can be turned into concrete next steps and suggest a clear course of action.
definition_2: The findings show exactly what the team should do next to improve the current process.
example: We need actionable insights from the user feedback to improve the app.

definition: To add value is to contribute something useful.
definition_2: This contribution gives the team something useful that improves the overall result.
example: That was a value-added comment you made.

definition: Officially announce the end of a meeting.
definition_2: His meetings officially ended the meeting after confirming there were no further questions.
example: Meeting adjourned.

definition: A list of topics that will be covered in the meeting.
definition_2: I shared the list of topics we will discuss during the meeting.
example: Make sure you send an agenda before the meeting to give people an idea of what to expect and so people have a chance to suggest changes.

definition: Ensure everyone agrees on the same direction.
definition_2: Everyone should agree on the same direction.
example: We need to align on priorities before the workshop.

definition: To align upon something is to agree on it.
definition_2: Let's agree on this before we move forward.
example: Let's align on the meeting agenda first.

definition: A shared understanding of a goal or purpose and how to work toward it together.
definition_2: We need everyone working from the same expectations, priorities, and overall direction.
example: I want to make sure we're all in alignment on the project goals.

definition: AP stands for Accounts Payable, which typically references the department inside of a company that is in charge of paying people the organization owes money to.
definition_2: The finance team responsible for paying the company’s outstanding bills is reviewing the invoice.
example: Your reimbursement is an AP of the company.

definition: Sorry for professionals who don't want to say sorry.
definition_2: Sorry about that.
example: Apologies for the delay in responding.

definition: AR stands for Accounts Receivable, which typically references the department inside of a company that is in charge of receiving money from people who owe the organization money.
definition_2: The finance team responsible for collecting money owed to the company is following up on the unpaid invoice.
example: Our AR is over the top.So many clients still haven't paid us for our services.

definition: ARR stands for Annual Recurring Revenue and is a popular metric used within the software and technology industry.It describes the amount of money a company can expect to predictably make each year through recurring subscriptions.
definition_2: How much recurring revenue we expect each year
example: People like subscription businesses because they generate ARR through user subscriptions.

definition: ASAP stands for As Soon As Possible and is a marker for something you should probably do immediately.
definition_2: As soon as you possibly can.
example: We need to respond to this ASAP.

term: At the end of the day
definition: At the end of the day means the most important consideration in the end.
definition_2: The most important consideration is whether the final outcome meets our goal.
example: At the end of the day no one is going to read this.

definition: B2B means Business to Business, which typically references a company that sells something to another organization.
definition_2: We sell to other companies not regular people.
example: This furniture company makes most of its money selling B2B.

definition: B2C means Business to Consumer, which typically references a company that sells something to an individual.
definition_2: We sell straight to everyday end customers.
example: This other furniture company primarily sells B2C to families and college students.

definition: When people meet privately with others to either gather information or to obtain someone's support for a decision.
definition_2: Some team members spoke privately to gather more information before the decision was made.
example: Let me do some back-channeling on this candidate to understand what they were like in their prior job.

definition: Something that is a lower priority or that is being postponed for later.
definition_2: Let’s postpone this until the higher-priority work is complete.
example: Let's put this project on the backburner for now.

definition: Refers to whoever is responsible for making the next move.
definition_2: She is now responsible for responding and deciding what happens next.
example: The ball is in the legal department's court.We need their approval before we can proceed.

definition: A person's capacity time or energy or availability to take on work.
definition_2: I'm swamped with everything right now.
example: I'm not sure I have bandwidth right now.

definition: To be bearish is to be pessimistic about a situation.
definition_2: The team is pessimistic about the market’s prospects over the coming months.
example: Investors are bearish on the stock market so are saving up dry powder.

definition: Something that hints at the potential beginning of a trend.
definition_2: Early sign that a trend might be starting.
example: The fact that so many customers are rating our product highly is a bellwether that this might be a hot product.

definition: Something to comparing performance against others.
definition_2: We should compare our performance with others to see how well we are doing.
example: 50% margin sounds high.Is this in line with industry benchmarks?

definition: Best practice(s) are ways of doing things that a company or industry has decided is the standard, most effective or efficient method, or widely accepted methods or techniques for achieving a goal.
definition_2: The way everyone in the industry does it.
example: In management consulting, it's considered best practice to make sure that every PowerPoint slide has a full sentence that summarizes what's shown on the slide itself.

definition: A major concept or innovative plan.
definition_2: We need a major concept that can shape the overall direction of the project.
example: We need a big idea to differentiate our brand.

term: Bite off more than you can chew
definition: Take on more than one can handle.
definition_2: He accepted too many responsibilities and now cannot handle them effectively.
example: Don't bite off more than you can chew on this project.

definition: Bite the bullet means suck it up and do something difficult.
definition_2: Just accept the difficulty and complete the task anyway.
example: Let's just bite the bullet and fire this person.

definition: To get approval from someone higher up.
definition_2: We need approval from senior leadership before moving forward.
example: This report has been blessed by the VP.

definition: The basic work needed to get something done.
definition_2: The basic grunt work that has to get done.
example: The last week was spent on the basic blocking and tackling.

definition: A new market where there is little to no competition.
definition_2: The strategy focuses on developing a market that other companies have not yet entered.
example: We need a blue ocean strategy because the ocean where we're playing is red.

definition: Brainstorming as many ideas as possible without thinking about whether something is actually possible.
definition_2: Generate as many ideas as possible without worrying yet about practical limits.
example: We need some blue sky thinking around here.

definition: A detailed plan or outline for a project.
definition_2: Detailed plan for how we'll execute.
example: This serves as the blueprint for future campaigns.

definition: Overcomplicate something by analyzing too many things at once.
definition_2: We are making this more complicated by trying to analyze every possible issue at once.
example: Just do this one calculation.Don't boil the ocean.

definition: The main point or final outcome.
definition_2: The main point is whether the project delivers the result we need.
example: The bottom line is that we need more time.

definition: To give another person all the files or knowledge that one holds.
definition_2: Let me transfer everything I know about this project before I step away.
example: Would you have 30 minutes to do a brain dump on this project before you leave for vacation?

definition: The point at which costs and revenues are equal.
definition_2: The project will cover all its costs once the revenue reaches the same amount as the expenses.
example: We need to break even by next quarter.

definition: To be bullish is to be optimistic about a situation.
definition_2: I'm optimistic this is going to work out.
example: Investors are bullish on the stock market so are deploying capital left and right.

definition: The rate at which money is spent.
definition_2: The company is tracking how quickly it spends its available funds.
example: Our burn rate is too high for this quarter.

definition: Work late into the night or working overtime.
definition_2: The team stayed late into the night to finish the work before the deadline.
example: We were burning the midnight oil to meet the deadline.

definition: Business case means sharing why it makes sense for a business to try something new.
definition_2: Explain why this plan make sense for a business.
example: If you are selling to a for-profit, the business case typically needs to be about how your solution will increase revenues and/or decrease costs.

definition: To get someone's endorsement on something.
definition_2: We need their support before moving forward with the proposal.
example: Submitting this proposal before getting the department heads' buy-in is a surefire way of getting nowhere.

definition: A certain routine or pattern.
definition_2: The team should follow a consistent routine for completing and reviewing the work.
example: Would you like to meet on a weekly cadence?

definition: Stop working for the day.
definition_2: Let’s stop working now and continue tomorrow.
example: Let's call it a day and continue tomorrow.

definition: CTA means Call to Action that whatever action or request or instruction you want the other person to take.
definition_2: The message should clearly state what the people needs to do next.
example: People aren't responding to your emails because you're sending big blocks of text without a clear CTA.

definition: A seemingly small issue that gets turned into a much bigger issue.
definition_2: This small issue could uncover a much larger and more complicated problem.
example: Let's not open that can of worms.

definition: Warning that some danger is ahead.
definition_2: The early warning signs suggest that a more serious problem may be approaching.
example: A lack of pre-orders may be a canary in the coalmine that this product will not sell well.

definition: Money or anything of value that enables a company to do its job.
definition_2: Enough money and valuable resources to continue operating effectively.
example: Financial capital is important, yes, but I'd argue that time is also a form of capital.

definition: Share information with others in a structured way.
definition_2: Please pass the update through a clear and organized way.
example: Please cascade the new policy to your teams.

definition: The movement of money in and out of a business.
definition_2: Money coming in and going out of the business.
example: Positive cash flow is critical for small businesses.

definition: The person in charge of orchestrating the meeting or leading a group of people.
definition_2: Who's running the meeting today?
example: Can you chair this meeting?

definition: Either a mentor who will advocate for you or a person who will push a project through to approval.
definition_2: We need someone who will advocate for the project and help move it through the approval process.
example: This project will die on the client side unless we find an internal champion who can own everything.

definition: You can use whatever information I'm about to tell you, but you didn't hear it from me.
definition_2: You may use the information shared here, but do not identify who provided it.
example: Chatham House Rules apply to this meeting.

definition: To contribute to a discussion.
definition_2: Please add your thoughts to the discussion when you have something useful to share.
example: Please chime in if you have any ideas.

definition: Refers to the loss of customers, users, subscribers, or clients over time.
definition_2: The company is losing customers faster than it can replace them.
example: When doing your due diligence on a potential employer, review their employee churn statistics.

definition: The percentage of customers, users, subscribers, or clients who stop using a service.
definition_2: The company is measuring the percentage of customers who stop using the service over a given period.
example: We need strategies to reduce our churn rate.

definition: To meet back or reconnect about a topic at a later time.
definition_2: Let’s reconnect later to continue discussing this topic.
example: Let's circle back once you've had a chance to draft something up.

definition: Come together to defend a shared position or idea.
definition_2: The team needs to come together and defend the decision with a united position.
example: Let's circle the wagons to address the criticism.

definition: Define and understands what is expected of them, including goals, responsibilities, deliverables, timelines, and success criteria.
definition_2: We need to make sure everyone understands their goals, responsibilities, deadlines, and required deliverables.
example: Let's clarify expectations before we proceed.

definition: Wrap up a topic or process with a firm conclusion.
definition_2: We need to finish this discussion with a clear decision and final next step.
example: Can you reach out to the client to close the loop on that proposal?

definition: COB means Close of Business, which typically means at the time office or business hours ends.
definition_2: Please send the completed report before office hours end today.
example: If someone tells you to get something to them by COB, they probably actually mean by 4:00pm.

definition: Joint work by multiple people or teams.
definition_2: This project requires several people to work together toward the same goal.
example: This success was a collaborative effort.

definition: Consult means to ask for someone's opinion.
definition_2: I’d like to ask for your opinion before we make the final decision.
example: You should consult your manager before sending out a mass email.

definition: The background information others need to have to understand your point.
definition_2: Please provide the background information needed to understand the situation.
example: Before you dive in with the numbers, provide the audience with some context behind your research.

definition: What we are really good at.
definition_2: This is one of the areas where our team great at and performs especially well.
example: Design is not our core competency.

definition: A calculation of the extent to which something is worth the effort.
definition_2: Expected advantages or benefit versus the money of effort required.
example: I conducted a cost-benefit analysis for my manager showing it's worth it to upgrade to the enterprise version.

definition: The essential steps that must be completed to finish a project.
definition_2: We need to identify the essential steps that must be completed for the project to finish on time.
example: Identifying the critical path helps you determine the minimum time needed to complete a project.

definition: Involving multiple teams or departments.
definition_2: The project requires people from several departments to work together.
example: This is a cross-functional initiative with marketing and sales.

definition: Sharing ideas or strategies between teams.
definition_2: The teams should exchange ideas so each group can learn from the other.
example: We can learn a lot from cross-pollination between departments.

definition: How well someone aligns with a company's values and practices.
definition_2: This person’s values and working style match how the company operates.
example: This candidate seems like a great culture fit.

definition: When customers actively promote a brand.
definition_2: Our customers actively recommend the brand to other people.
example: Our customer advocacy program encourages referrals.

definition: The full experience a customer has with a brand.
definition_2: Every step a customer goes through with us.
example: Mapping the customer journey helps us identify pain points.

definition: The ability to keep existing customers.
definition_2: The company needs to keep its existing customers from leaving.
example: Improving customer retention is our top priority.

definition: Focused on meeting customer needs and expectations.
definition_2: Put the customer at the center of every decision.
example: We need to adopt a more customer-centric approach.

definition: Do something in the easiest or cheapest way.
definition_2: The team chose the easiest approach instead of completing the work properly.
example: We can't cut corners when it comes to quality.

definition: Focus on what's important amidst distractions.
definition_2: Let’s focus on the most important information and ignore the surrounding distractions.
example: We need this campaign to cut through the noise in the market.

definition: Get straight to the point.
definition_2: Skip the fluff and tell what's the main point.
example: Let's cut to the chase and discuss the main issue.

definition: CYA means Cover Your Ass, to do something so that you don't get blamed for something later.
definition_2: Please document the decision so there is a record of who approved it.
example: You should write down what you agreed upon in email as a CYA move.

definition: Making decisions based on data analysis.
definition_2: We should base the decision on evidence from the available information.
example: We need a data-driven approach for marketing.

definition: A presentation slide deck, usually created in PowerPoint, Google Slides, Keynote, or similar tools.
definition_2: Please prepare a set of presentation slides for the upcoming meeting.
example: Please update this deck with the latest numbers.

definition: A detailed, thorough examination of a topic, problem, project, or dataset, and to look into something more closely.
definition_2: We need to examine this topic deeper in detail rather than reviewing it only at a high level.
example: Let's do a deep dive on this topic tomorrow.

definition: To exceed a customer's expectations and create a positive, memorable experience and not just satisfy them.
definition_2: Go above and beyond what the customer expect.
example: Our goal is to delight the customer at every touchpoint.

definition: Anything that needs to be produced.
definition_2: Define exactly what must be completed and submitted.
example: The deliverable is a 10-page report.

definition: The difference.
definition_2: We need to identify the difference between the current result and the expected outcome.
example: The delta between the top-selling product and the second best selling product is massive.

definition: Derisk (or de-risk) means to take proactive steps to make the outcome of a decision more certain.
definition_2: We should take preventive steps now to reduce uncertainty around the final outcome.
example: Many successful companies were actually started as side hustles.These entrepreneurs derisked their idea before going all in.

definition: A term used to describe the people who work under a given manager.
definition_2: The manager is responsible for supervising the employees who work directly under them.
example: Psychological safety with your direct reports is so important.

definition: To significantly change an industry, market, or way of doing things by innovating or introducing something new.
definition_2: The new approach could significantly change how the entire industry operates.
example: We're poised to disrupt the healthcare technology market.

definition: An innovation that significantly changes how industries, businesses, or consumers operate, often replacing older technologies or business models.
definition_2: Tech that completely changes how an industry works
example: AI is the most disruptive technology of our time.

definition: To start something immediately, right away, without spending much time on introductions, preparation, or discussion.
definition_2: Let’s start the work immediately without spending too much time on introductions.
example: Let's dive right in.What do you need?

definition: A situation where two people work with each other, but neither has managerial authority over the other.
definition_2: You work with them but they don't manage you.
example: I am dotted line to Eric and solid line to Lea.

definition: To increase commitment, investment, effort, or focus on something because you believe it will succeed or is strategically important.
definition_2: Put more focus and resources into this.
example: We need to double down on marketing efforts.

definition: Dig deeper into a topic or issue.
definition_2: Let’s take a closer look at this issue before deciding on the next step.
example: I want to double-click on your feedback about engagement surveys.

definition: Give information to other team members.
definition_2: I’ll share the key details with the team so everyone has the same context.
example: We're here to download last week's investor call.

definition: To examine something in greater detail by breaking it down into smaller parts, focus on details or specifics.
definition_2: We should break this issue into smaller pieces so we can understand the details more clearly.
example: We need to drill down into these metrics to find the issue.

definition: To screw up, make a mistake, forget something important, or fail to handle a responsibility properly.
definition_2: I missed an important responsibility and it caused an issue for the team.
example: Good job not dropping the ball on that presentation.

definition: Extra, unused resources, especially money.
definition_2: We still have extra budget available if the team needs support later.
example: We have plenty of dry powder left for the upcoming quarter.

definition: To prepare everything necessary.
definition_2: We should make sure everything is prepared before we move forward with the plan.
example: Let's meet with the VP once we have our ducks in a row.

definition: Research to try and understand how legitimate something is.
definition_2: We should research this carefully before deciding whether it is legitimate.
example: I haven't done my due diligence on this candidate, but if you have, I'll trust your opinion.

definition: EA means Executive Assistant, a professional who supports senior leaders.
definition_2: The senior leader’s support professional can help coordinate the schedule and manage key follow-ups.
example: When setting up a meeting with someone important, work with that person's EA.

definition: An uncomfortable topic people would rather not discuss.
definition_2: We need to address the uncomfortable topic that everyone has been avoiding.
example: That was a useless meeting.People never once addressed the elephant in the room.

definition: The level of commitment and enthusiasm employees feel.
definition_2: The team seems genuinely committed to the work and excited about contributing to the company’s goals.
example: Employee engagement is key to retaining talent.

definition: Give authority or confidence to others.
definition_2: We should give the team more authority to make decisions without waiting for constant approval.
example: Our goal is to empower employees to make decisions.

definition: To actively involve, interact with, attract, or gain participation from someone.
definition_2: We need to actively involve the team so they participate in the discussion.
example: Don't forget to engage with the other team.

definition: EOD means End of Day or by the end of the business day.
definition_2: Please send the update before the business day ends.
example: I will get back to you by EOD.

definition: EOM means End of Message, an acronym people put on a short message to signal that they are done.
definition_2: The message is complete, so there is no additional context to read.
example: Can you come to my office? EOM.

definition: EOW means End of Week or by the end of the current work week usually by Friday close of business..
definition_2: Please complete the review before the current work week ends.
example: I will get back to you by EOW.

definition: ETA means Estimated Time of Arrival or the expected time when someone or something will arrive at a destination.
definition_2: Do we have an expected arrival time for the files or the person we are waiting on?
example: What's your ETA?

definition: To make a decision yourself without putting a topic up for a group vote.
definition_2: I’ll make the call on this so we can move forward without waiting for a group vote.
example: Don't waste people's time with a long poll.Just make an executive decision.

definition: A bullet point list of the most important information, usually presented at the front of a long deck.
definition_2: Please put the most important points at the front so the team can understand the deck quickly.
example: When explaining ideas to people, start with the executive summary, then pause and let others react.

definition: Lead or guide a discussion or meeting.
definition_2: Can you guide the meeting and help keep the conversation focused?
example: Who will facilitate today's brainstorming session?

definition: Quickly identify and learn from mistakes.
definition_2: We should test the idea quickly so we can learn from any mistakes early.
example: Our strategy is to fail fast and iterate.

definition: Predicting future trends or performance.
definition_2: We need to predict future performance so the team can plan more accurately.
example: We're forecasting a 10% increase in sales.

definition: Revealing all relevant information about a situation, decision, transaction, or relationship, rather than withholding important facts.
definition_2: I want to share all the relevant details so nothing important is left out.
example: Full disclosure: I know that candidate personally.

definition: Making something sustainable or relevant for the future.
definition_2: We should design this in a way that stays useful as our needs change over time.
example: We need to future-proof our technology.

definition: FYI means For Your Information, information you are sharing that people don't need to reply to.
definition_2: I’m sharing this update so you have the information, but no response is needed.
example: FYI, the 2pm meeting has moved to room 203.

definition: Start making progress, gaining acceptance, attracting attention, or building momentum.
definition_2: The idea is starting to make progress and more people are beginning to support it.
example: The product is finally gaining traction in new markets.

definition: Something that dramatically impacts a situation.
definition_2: This could have a major impact on how we handle the situation.
example: This marketing strategy is a game changer.

definition: A detailed strategy or plan for achieving a goal.
definition_2: We need a clear strategy that explains how we will reach the goal.
example: We need a game plan for the product launch.

definition: Gantt chart means a chart that shows tasks and timelines for a project.
definition_2: Can you share a visual schedule that shows each task and its timeline?
example: Please put this project plan on a Gantt chart so that we can visually see all the overlapping tasks.

definition: To gain a general understanding or feel for something before having all the details.
definition_2: I want to understand the general direction before we get into the details.
example: Let's get a sense of the team's opinion on this matter.

definition: Focus on the essential facts or practical details of a matter, especially after preliminary discussion.
definition_2: We should focus on the key facts and practical details now.
example: Let's get down to brass tacks and finalize the project plan.

definition: Get the ball rolling means to start something.
definition_2: We should start this work now so the team can make progress.
example: James, how about you get the ball rolling by giving your update first?

term: Get your ducks in a row
definition: Get organized and be prepared.
definition_2: Please make sure everything is prepared before we move ahead.
example: Before the meeting, let’s get our ducks in a row.

definition: To provide advance notice or a warning about something before it happens.
definition_2: Please let the team know in advance so they are not surprised later.
example: Just a heads up that I will be on vacation starting tomorrow.

definition: Going forward means from this point on, from now on, in the future, and moving ahead.
definition_2: From now on, we should use this process for all similar requests.
example: Going forward, Jen will be your main contact.

definition: Very detailed, specific, or broken down into smaller parts.
definition_2: Can you provide more detailed information instead of only the high-level view?
example: This explanation is too vague.Can you be more granular?

definition: Approve something to move forward.
definition_2: Leadership approved the project, so the team can move ahead.
example: The team has greenlighted the proposal.

definition: An instinctive judgment or intuition, made without having all the data or analysis.
definition_2: My instinct is that this option is the right direction, even without complete data.
example: What's your gut feel towards this color scheme?

definition: Hard copy means a print-out of a document.
definition_2: Can you bring a printed version of the document to the meeting?
example: Can you give me the next draft in hard copy?

definition: Hard stop means a time when I definitely need to leave.
definition_2: I definitely need to leave at 3 p.m., so we should cover the key points first.
example: I'd love to chat, but I have a hard stop at 2:25pm.

definition: Has legs means has potential idea, project, strategy, or trend has the potential to succeed, grow, or remain relevant over time.
definition_2: This idea has real potential to grow if we keep building on it.
example: This idea may have legs.Let's bring it up in our next team meeting.

definition: Headwinds means situations or factors that make something move more slowly or decline.
definition_2: We are facing some challenges that could slow down progress.
example: Falling gas prices are a headwind to gas companies that want to make more money.

definition: High level means the broad, strategic, summary-level, without going into detailed specifics you want to explain.
definition_2: Can you give me the broad summary without going into all the details yet?
example: Just tell me the high level takeaway right now.

definition: HiPPO means the Highest Paid Person's Opinion or Highest Paid Person in the Office.
definition_2: We should not let the most senior person’s opinion outweigh the data.
example: Just sit and take notes.It's all up to the HiPPO.

definition: Hit the ground running means to be useful right away without needing help.
definition_2: We need someone who can contribute immediately without a long onboarding period.
example: Can you meet with Carl so he can hit the ground running?

definition: Looking ahead to identify future risks or opportunities.
definition_2: We should look ahead and identify future risks before they affect the team.
example: We're horizon scanning for upcoming market trends.

definition: Hypothesis means your guess as to what will happen given what you know about the situation.
definition_2: My current guess is that the new process will reduce delays.
example: Before you begin analyzing any data, come up with a hypothesis.

definition: Generate new ideas usually through brainstorming.
definition_2: Let’s generate a few new ideas before choosing a direction.
example: Let’s pull the team together and ideate ways to improve retention.

definition: The process of brainstorming new ideas.
definition_2: The team needs time to brainstorm possible solutions before we make a decision.
example: We'll have an ideation session this Friday.

definition: In a difficult situation, facing a problem, or under pressure with limited good options.
definition_2: We are in a difficult situation with limited options right now.
example: We're in a bind with the project deadline approaching.

definition: Summarize briefly, the short version.
definition_2: The short version is that we need to reduce costs and improve delivery speed.
example: In a nutshell, the project is on track for completion.

definition: In control of a situation.
definition_2: The team is now in control of the decision and can set the direction.
example: We are now in the driver's seat with this project.

definition: In the loop means to be included in the conversation or made aware.
definition_2: Please keep me included in the conversation as the plan changes.
example: Keep me in the loop on how things go.

definition: In the pipeline means things that people expect to happen or tasks that people expect to do.
definition_2: There are several tasks expected to come through over the next few weeks.
example: What new product features do we have in the pipeline?

definition: The center of attention.
definition_2: This project is getting a lot of attention from leadership right now.
example: Our CEO is in the spotlight during this interview.

definition: In your wheelhouse means your specialty.
definition_2: This task fits your area of expertise, so you would be the right person to handle it.
example: Python isn't quite in my wheelhouse.

definition: Incentivize means to give someone a reason to do something.
definition_2: We should give people a clear reason to participate in the new process.
example: $20 gift cards could help incentivize people to take our survey.

definition: Incremental innovation is the process of making small, continuous improvements to existing products, services, processes, or business models rather than creating entirely new breakthroughs.
definition_2: We should improve the existing process through small changes over time.
example: gradual improvements.

definition: Inherit means to take over for someone else.
definition_2: I will take over this responsibility from the person who managed it before.
example: I am inheriting John's financial model.

definition: A place or group focused on creating new ideas or technologies.
definition_2: The team needs a dedicated space for developing new ideas and technologies.
example: Our office will be an innovation hub for product design.

definition: Institutional memory means the history and processes of an organization that employees know but may not write down.
definition_2: A lot of important company knowledge exists in people’s experience rather than in written documents.
example: Half of my org quit last week, so we have zero institutional memory now.

definition: Iterate means to work on multiple versions of something until it is perfect.
definition_2: We should keep improving the draft through multiple versions until it works well.
example: Don't just send me the final version.Let's iterate upon this together.

definition: Have a quick phone call or video meeting to discuss something.
definition_2: Can we have a quick meeting to talk through the issue?
example: I'll jump on a call with the team to discuss the issue.

definition: Keep someone informed about updates.
definition_2: Please keep me informed as new updates come in.
example: Keep me in the loop on the status of the project.

term: Keep your ear to the ground
definition: Stay informed or aware of developments.
definition_2: We should stay aware of any changes that could affect the project.
example: Keep your ear to the ground for any new updates.

definition: Key takeaway means the main point, idea, decision, or summary.
definition_2: The main point is that we need to simplify the process before launching it.
example: When others ask you for the key takeaways, first summarize everything into a single sentence.

term: Kick the can down the road
definition: Postpone a decision.
definition_2: We should not delay this decision again because the issue will only get harder.
example: We can't keep kicking the can down the road on this budget issue.

definition: Information isolated within one team or department.
definition_2: Important information is stuck within one team and not reaching the rest of the organization.
example: We need to break down knowledge silos to improve communication.

definition: Sharing expertise or information with others.
definition_2: We need to share the team’s expertise so others can continue the work smoothly.
example: We'll do a knowledge transfer session after the training.

definition: KPI means Key Performance Indicators, a metrics or measurable values used to track how effectively an individual, team, or organization is achieving its objectives.
definition_2: We should define measurable indicators to track whether the team is meeting its goals.
example: Revenue growth is one of our key KPIs.

definition: Take the lead on an initiative.
definition_2: Can you take ownership of this initiative and guide the team through the next steps?
example: She will lead the charge on the sustainability project.

definition: Level set means to go over a topic so that everyone has the same understanding.
definition_2: Let’s review the topic together so everyone has the same understanding before we continue.
example: Since not everyone was able to attend last week's meeting, let's begin by level setting.

definition: Improve or advance in skill or position.
definition_2: The team needs to improve its skills so we can handle more complex work.
example: We need to level up our customer service strategies.

definition: Leverage means to use something effectively to gain an advantage or achieve a goal.
definition_2: We should use the existing data more effectively to make a better decision.
example: Leverage the people around you.Don't be afraid to ask questions.

definition: Loop in means to include or involve someone in a conversation.
definition_2: Please include the finance team in this conversation so they have the full context.
example: Mind looping me in on the email thread? CC me.

definition: Low-hanging fruit means something that's easy to do yet makes an impact.
definition_2: Let’s start with the easiest tasks that can still create a meaningful impact.
example: Let's complete the low-hanging fruit tasks before tackling the harder ones.

definition: Set realistic goals or outcomes.
definition_2: We should be clear about what is realistic so the team knows what to expect.
example: Let's manage expectations with the client about delivery timelines.

definition: Material means substantial enough that people will notice.
definition_2: This change is significant enough that stakeholders will notice the difference.
example: Changing this assumption is material to the company's growth.

definition: Metric means a number or measurement used to track performance.
definition_2: We need a clear measurement to track whether performance is improving.
example: Our key performance metric is customer satisfaction.

definition: Come together to share ideas and perspectives.
definition_2: Let’s come together to share ideas and understand each other’s perspectives.
example: Let's have a quick mind meld before the client meeting tomorrow.

definition: Mission critical (or mission-critical) means the most important task that will make or break something.
definition_2: This task is essential and could determine whether the project succeeds.
example: We are in a hurry.Don't worry about anything that is not mission critical.

definition: An ambitious, risky project or idea, high-risk, high reward goal.
definition_2: This is an ambitious idea with high risk, but it could create a major reward.
example: This is a moonshot project, but it’s worth pursuing.

definition: Change objectives during a project.
definition_2: The objectives changed during the project, which made it harder to measure success.
example: They keep moving the goalposts

definition: Move the needle means something substantial enough that people will notice.
definition_2: This change could create a noticeable improvement in the final result.
example: This decision will move the needle.

definition: Net-net means the final result after everything is taken into account.
definition_2: After considering everything, the final result is still positive for the team.
example: Net-net, it was worthwhile to attend that conference.

definition: No worries means don't worry about it.
definition_2: Please do not stress about it; we can handle the issue later.
example: No worries, I've made the same mistake before.

definition: A guiding principle or ultimate goal or long-term success.
definition_2: The team needs a clear long-term goal to guide every decision we make.
example: Customer satisfaction is our North Star.

definition: Off the record means to discuss something without the conversation being recorded or shared.
definition_2: Can we discuss this privately without sharing it beyond this conversation?
example: Let's keep this conversation off the record.

definition: No longer available or being considered.
definition_2: That option is no longer being considered for this project.
example: That option is now off the table.

definition: Offline means not reachable.
definition_2: I will be unavailable for a few hours, so I may not respond right away.
example: I will be offline during my hiking trip.

definition: On board means to be in agreement with or aligned with the plan.
definition_2: The team is aligned with the plan and ready to move forward.
example: Make sure that Claire is on board with the email before sending it out.

definition: On my radar means something you want to draw someone's attention to.
definition_2: I wanted to bring this issue to your attention before it becomes urgent.
example: I wanted to put this on your radar.

definition: Undecided between two or more options or not yet ready to make a decision.
definition_2: I have not decided which option is better yet.
example: I'm still on the fence about this decision.

definition: A topic or issue to be aware of, something is known, being watched, or under consideration but not necessarily the top priority right now.
definition_2: This topic is being watched, even though it is not the top priority right now.
example: This bug fix is on the radar for next quarter.

definition: On the same page means to be in agreement or have a common understanding on a topic.
definition_2: Let’s make sure everyone has the same understanding before we continue.
example: Make sure that you and your manager are on the same page before you start the assignment.

definition: The process of bringing someone (or something) into an organization and getting them set up to work effectively.
definition_2: The new hire needs a clear process to get set up and work effectively.
example: We need to streamline the onboarding process for new hires.

definition: OOO means Out of Office, typically when someone is on vacation or not available.
definition_2: I will be away from work tomorrow and may not respond until I return.
example: Make sure you set an email OOO greeting before you go on vacation.

definition: Reveal information or plans.
definition_2: We need to reveal more of the plan so the team understands what is happening.
example: It's time to open the kimono and share our strategy.

definition: Opportunity cost refers to what you're losing out on by making a certain decision.
definition_2: We need to consider what we give up by choosing this option.
example: Sure, you could go back to school, but think about the opportunity cost.

definition: Optics means how people perceive the situation.
definition_2: The situation could be perceived poorly by people who are not involved in the details.
example: It's bad optics if the intern presents to the client.

definition: Optimize means to find the most efficient or effective method of achieving a certain goal.
definition_2: We should make this process more efficient so the team can reach the goal with less effort.
example: If you find yourself doing the same thing multiple times, try to optimize your approach.

definition: To be unreachable.
definition_2: I will be unavailable tomorrow afternoon and may not respond right away.
example: I'll be out of pocket tomorrow afternoon for my daughter's dance recital.

definition: Out of the box (out-of-the-box) means think creatively or unconventionally.
definition_2: We need a creative approach instead of relying on the usual solution.
example: We need out-of-the-box thinking to solve this issue.

definition: Outside the box means think creatively or unconventionally.
definition_2: We may need a fresh and creative solution rather than the usual process.
example: We need an outside-the-box solution for this problem.

definition: Shift responsibility to another person or team.
definition_2: Please do not pass this issue to another team without helping resolve it first.
example: Let's not throw this issue over the fence without resolving it.

definition: Overhead refers to all ongoing financial costs needed to keep operations running.
definition_2: These are the ongoing costs we have to cover just to keep the business running.
example: Wow, you live a high overhead life with this fancy house and fancy car!

definition: Ownership mindset is the belief that you own every aspect of a project from start to finish.
definition_2: I need everyone to treat this project as something they are responsible for from start to finish.
example: Few members of our workforce have an ownership mindset.Most just wait around to be told what to do.

definition: A specific problem faced by customers.
definition_2: Customers are clearly struggling with this specific problem, so we should address it directly.
example: Our product solves a major pain point for small businesses.

definition: Paradigm shift means something that fundamentally changes people's thinking.
definition_2: This change would fundamentally alter how people think about the work.
example: This could completely reshape our assumptions about how the business should function.

definition: Postpone discussing a topic for another time.
definition_2: Let’s pause this topic for now and return to it in a later discussion.
example: Let's park that idea and revisit it later.

definition: Pencil in means to roughly agree on a date.
definition_2: Let’s tentatively reserve Monday afternoon and confirm the exact time later.
example: Let's pencil in next Monday at 2pm and we can confirm on the morning of.

definition: Pick your brain means to ask for your perspective.
definition_2: I’d like to get your perspective on this before I make a decision.
example: I'd love to pick your brain about this new project.

definition: Take inspiration from an existing idea or initiative
definition_2: We can build on the existing initiative instead of starting from nothing.
example: rather than start from scratch

definition: Send a brief message or notification to someone.
definition_2: I’ll send Sean a quick message to check whether he has an update.
example: I'll ping Sean to check in.

definition: Ping someone means to contact someone.
definition_2: Please contact me tomorrow afternoon and we can discuss the details then.
example: Ping me tomorrow at 2pm and we can chat then.

definition: Pivot means to change directions, especially when it comes to a business's strategy or focus.
definition_2: We need to change direction based on what we learned from customers.
example: After further market research, we realized our most avid customers are actually immigration lawyers, so we pivoted from B2C to B2B.

definition: Argue against an idea to test its validity.
definition_2: I’m going to argue the other side so we can test whether the idea holds up.
example: I’m trying to help the team see what might go wrong."

definition: POC means Point of Contact which the person you go to for a specific topic, project, vendor, or issue.
definition_2: Who is the right person to contact about this vendor issue?
example: Who is the right POC for this initiative?

definition: POV means Point of View or someone's opinion.
definition_2: My view is that we should wait until the results are stronger before asking for more budget.
example: My POV is that it's too early to ask for a raise.

definition: Pressure test means to find weak points to an argument or something that was overlooked.
definition_2: Let’s test the assumptions carefully so we can find any weak points in the analysis.
example: Have you pressure-tested the assumptions in your Excel analysis?

definition: Taking action before a problem arises.
definition_2: We should address customer concerns before they become bigger problems.
example: We need to be proactive about addressing customer concerns.

definition: A test to demonstrate feasibility and show an idea can work before full investment.
definition_2: We should run a small test first to show the idea can work before funding the full rollout.
example: We're building a proof of concept before the full rollout.

definition: Postpone or to delay, avoid, or push a decision or problem to later often because it’s hard, risky, or no one wants to own it right now.
definition_2: Let’s delay the decision until next week because we do not have enough information yet.
example: Let's punt that to next week's meeting.

definition: Push back means to give a counterargument, resist, disagree, or challenge something.
definition_2: I have some concerns about the proposal and want to challenge a few assumptions.
example: My only push-back to this idea is that it will take more than six months before we know if it will work.

definition: Temporarily set aside a topic or decision.
definition_2: Let’s temporarily set this decision aside until we have more information.
example: We'll put a pin in this until we can get more information.

term: Put it on the back burner
definition: To deprioritize something for now when still keep it in mind, but don’t focus on it actively.
definition_2: This should be a lower priority for now, but we should keep it in mind.
example: Let's put this issue on the back burner for now.

definition: Make a good impression.
definition_2: Let’s show up prepared so we make a strong impression in the client meeting.
example: Let's put our best foot forward in the client meeting tomorrow.

definition: QC means Quality Control, or to double-check something to make sure it works and there are no mistakes.
definition_2: Please double-check the report for mistakes before we send it to the client.
example: Let's QC this report one more time before sending it out.

definition: Quarter means a three month period in a company's financial calendar.
definition_2: Sales improved during the most recent three-month reporting period.
example: Our sales increased by 20% in Q1.

definition: Quick win(s) means a small and fast accomplishment or easy success.
definition_2: Fixing this small issue would give the team a fast success before launch.
example: Fixing this bug would be a quick win for the launch.

definition: Increase standards or expectations.
definition_2: We need to increase our standards for product quality going forward.
example: We need to raise the bar on product quality.

definition: Motivate and gather the team for a purpose.
definition_2: Let’s bring the team together and motivate everyone for the year-end goal.
example: Let's rally the troops to hit our year-end goals.

definition: Red tape means bureaucracy.
definition_2: The approval process is slowed down by too many administrative steps.
example: The approval involves a lot of red tape.

definition: Reinvent the wheel means to redo something from scratch rather than make use of other people's work.
definition_2: We should not redo the work from scratch when a useful template already exists.
example: When starting a new assignment, resist the urge to reinvent the wheel.

definition: To connect with, appeal to, or have a strong impact on an audience, customer, stakeholder, or employee.
definition_2: The message needs to connect more strongly with the audience.
example: Please see below for my list of questions.Does this resonate?

definition: RFP means Request for Proposal, when an organization announces they would like other organizations to send them a plan for solving a problem.
definition_2: The company is asking vendors to send plans for how they would solve the problem.
example: This RFP is super long.

definition: Roadmap means a plan, calendar, or timeline, a high-level plan that shows what you intend to do over time.
definition_2: We need a high-level timeline that shows what the team plans to deliver over time.
example: Before you hide away for a month, present your roadmap to your manager.

definition: ROI means Return on Investment, how much benefit you get for putting in a certain amount of money or time, an investment relative to its cost.
definition_2: We need to compare the benefit of this project against the money and time required.
example: Let's rank these initiatives by their ROI.

definition: Present an idea to see how others respond.
definition_2: Let’s present the idea informally and see how people respond before committing.
example: Let's run this up the flagpole with leadership.

definition: Runway means how much time you have left before running out of resources.
definition_2: At our current spending rate, we only have a few months before the money runs out.
example: My startup only has a four-month runway, so I should really start fundraising.

definition: Scalable means something can grow bigger fast without breaking anything or without costs or complexity.
definition_2: The process should be able to grow quickly without breaking or becoming too expensive.
example: Allowing every customer to speak with a human within 10 seconds is not scalable.

definition: Expand a team, product, service, or business, ideally to do it efficiently.
definition_2: We need to expand the service efficiently as demand grows.
example: We need this process to scale along with our team.

definition: Scope means the boundaries for a project, where in-scope represents tasks one should do and out-of-scope represents irrelevant tasks.
definition_2: Please clarify which tasks are included in this project and which ones are not.
example: Is pricing in scope for this conversation?

definition: Process or experience that is smooth and efficient.
definition_2: The user should be able to complete the process smoothly without extra friction.
example: Our checkout experience should be seamless.

definition: Socialize means sharing an idea with others to get their endorsement before a big group decision is made.
definition_2: We should share the idea with key people first so they can support it before the big meeting.
example: Make sure you socialize an idea around the team before you present it in a big meeting.

definition: SOW means Scope of Work or Statement of Work, a contract that states what work needs to be done by when.
definition_2: The contract needs to state exactly what work will be done and by when.
example: Can you please draft an SOW with our partners for me to review?

definition: When someone appears who was just being talked about.
definition_2: We were just talking about her, and now she has joined the call.
example: Ah, speak of the devil! Here’s John now!

definition: Stakeholder(s) means anyone impacted by or invested in a project or decision.
definition_2: Please include everyone who is affected by this decision in the update.
example: We need to update stakeholders about the delay.

definition: Take responsibility or initiative and act when something needs to be done.
definition_2: Someone needs to take initiative and handle this before the deadline slips.
example: We need someone to step up to the plate and lead this project.

definition: Means everyone and everything is pointed and works in the same direction as the same goals.
definition_2: All teams need to work toward the same goals instead of moving in different directions.
example: We need strategic alignment before the launch.

definition: Strategic fit means how well something matches the company’s long-term goals, direction, and strengths.
definition_2: This partnership makes sense only if it supports our long-term goals and strengths.
example: This initiative is a strategic fit for our company vision.

definition: Strawman (straw-man) means a rough first draft or outline of something just to start discussion and not a final plan.
definition_2: I drafted a rough outline so the team has something concrete to react to.
example: Don't just hide away for weeks and come back with a 20-page report.Give your manager a strawman first.

definition: Bring attention to a problem.
definition_2: I want to bring this problem to everyone’s attention before it gets worse.
example: Please surface any issues during the beta testing.

definition: Swim lanes means whatever you are responsible for.
definition_2: That task belongs to your area of responsibility, so please handle the next step.
example: Samir needs to stay in his swim lane and stop doing other people's tasks.

definition: Synergy means some extra benefit arising from two things being combined.
definition_2: Combining the two teams could create more value than each one working separately.
example: Since our teams are working on similar topics, there are a lot of synergies from us sitting close to each other.

definition: Synthesize means to look at the situation as a whole and summarize the main points.
definition_2: Please review the full situation and summarize the main points for leadership.
example: Can you synthesize this whitepaper?

definition: Table means to postpone discussion on a topic in a meeting.
definition_2: Let’s postpone this topic and return to it in a later meeting.
example: Let's table this issue for now because we are running short on time.

definition: Table stakes means the bare minimum expectation or baseline requirements.
definition_2: Following the basic instructions is the minimum expectation for this role.
example: Following instructions is table stakes in a new job.

definition: Tailwinds means situations or external factors that make something grow or increase.
definition_2: Current market conditions are helping the business grow faster than expected.
example: Falling gas prices are a tailwind to trucking companies because it costs less money to fuel their trucks.

definition: Discuss later outside the current meeting.
definition_2: Let’s discuss this privately after the meeting instead of using the group’s time.
example: We’re short on time, so let’s take it offline.

definition: Handle something gradually or in stages.
definition_2: Let’s handle one issue at a time instead of trying to fix everything at once.
example: We'll take it step by step and address each issue carefully.

definition: Be accountable for something.
definition_2: Please be accountable for this task and make sure it gets completed.
example: We need team members to take ownership of their tasks.

definition: Be in charge or take responsibility.
definition_2: I can be in charge of organizing the event and coordinating the next steps.
example: I'll take the lead on organizing this event.

definition: Take this offline means let's follow up one-on-one later rather than discuss in front of everyone.
definition_2: Let’s continue this conversation one-on-one after the meeting.
example: Let's take this offline.

definition: Ensuring all team members are on the same page.
definition_2: The team needs a shared understanding of the goals before we start executing.
example: We need better team alignment for this initiative.

definition: Someone who works well in a team setting.
definition_2: We need someone who collaborates well and helps the group succeed.
example: We're looking for a team player for this role.

definition: The set of technologies used in a project.
definition_2: Which technologies, tools, and frameworks are we using to build this platform?
example: What's our tech stack for this platform?

definition: Plan for the future or anticipate.
definition_2: We need to plan for future demand instead of reacting only to today’s issues.
example: We need to think ahead to stay competitive in the market.

definition: Approach something creatively.
definition_2: We need a creative approach rather than repeating the usual marketing tactics.
example: We need to think outside the box for this marketing strategy.

definition: Consider something carefully and completely before deciding to acting.
definition_2: Let’s consider the options carefully before making a decision.
example: Let's think through the options before deciding.

definition: Someone recognized for expertise in a field.
definition_2: She is widely recognized as an expert whose ideas influence the field.
example: She's a thought leader in digital marketing.

definition: Touch base means to check in with someone briefly, usually to share an update, align, or follow up.
definition_2: Let’s have a quick check-in about the report after lunch.
example: Let's touch base about this report.

definition: Interaction with a customer or user.
definition_2: Every interaction a customer has with us should be clear and helpful.
example: We need to improve every touchpoint in the customer journey.

definition: Traction means real evidence that something is gaining momentum either with customers, revenue, usage, adoption, interest, or progress that shows it’s actually working.
definition_2: We are seeing real evidence that customers are starting to adopt the product.
example: Our tweet is getting traction on the Internet.

definition: Being open and honest.
definition_2: We should be open and honest about how this decision was made.
example: We value transparency in our decision-making process.

definition: Triangulate means to arrive at an estimate by piecing together a bunch of available data points.
definition_2: We can estimate the number by combining several available data points.
example: I triangulated customer traffic by multiplying November's traffic by 1.2.

definition: Turnover is the business way of saying quit.A high turnover organization has a high rate of employees quitting.
definition_2: The company has a high rate of employees leaving, which may signal a retention problem.
example: Review their employee turnover statistics when doing your due diligence on a potential employer.

definition: UI means User Interface, whatever the user touches or interacts with.
definition_2: The screen layout and buttons should be easier for users to understand.
example: The UI looks like it was made in the 90s.

definition: Something going unnoticed.
definition_2: This problem has been going unnoticed for too long.
example: The problem has been under the radar for a while.

definition: Feeling ill or unwell.
definition_2: She is feeling sick today and will not be able to join the meeting.
example: She's feeling a bit under the weather and won't be in today.

definition: Unpack means to explain or examine in more detail.
definition_2: Can you explain this concept in more detail so the team understands it?
example: Mind unpacking this concept for me?

definition: The potential for profit or benefit.
definition_2: There is strong potential benefit if this investment performs well.
example: There's significant upside in this investment.

definition: Learning new skills to improve performance.
definition_2: We are training the team so they can build new capabilities and perform better.
example: We're focused on upskilling our marketing team.

definition: Make use of something or put a resource, tool, or capability to work effectively.
definition_2: We should make effective use of the resources we already have.
example: How can we better utilize the team's talents?

definition: UX means User Experience, the process that a user takes to do something.
definition_2: The process has too many steps and makes it hard for users to complete the task.
example: The UX of this form is terrible.There are so many buttons I need to click.

definition: Improvement that increases the worth of a product.
definition_2: This feature adds a meaningful benefit that makes the product more worthwhile.
example: This feature is a real value add for our customers.

definition: Value prop stands for Value Proposition and it means the unique benefit a product or service provides.
definition_2: We need to explain the unique benefit customers get from this product.
example: What's the value proposition for this feature?

definition: VoC stands for Voice of The Customer and it means the feedback and insights directly from customers.
definition_2: We should listen closely to feedback that comes directly from customers.
example: We need to listen to the voice of the customer.

definition: Take on various roles or responsibilities.
definition_2: In a small company, people often have to handle several different responsibilities.
example: In a startup, you’ll need to wear multiple hats.

definition: Area of expertise, strength, skills.
definition_2: Excel modeling is not really my area of expertise.
example: Excel formulas aren't really in my wheelhouse.

definition: White-glove service refers to a premium, highly personalized level of customer service in which the provider handles most or all details for the customer, often with extra care, attention, and convenience.
definition_2: The client expects a premium level of personalized support with every detail handled carefully.
example: high-touch customer service.

definition: Something hat benefits all parties involved.
definition_2: This partnership benefits both companies, so it is worth pursuing.
example: This partnership is a win-win for both companies.

definition: Having a healthy balance between your job responsibilities and your personal life, so work does not consistently take over your time, energy, health, or relationships.
definition_2: We want employees to have enough time and energy for life outside work.
example: We prioritize work-life balance for our team.

definition: A collaborative session to brainstorm or solve problems.
definition_2: Let’s hold a collaborative working session to brainstorm solutions together.
example: We're hosting a workshop to improve team communication.

definition: YTD means Year to Date, the time between January 1st of this year and now.
definition_2: Please report the cumulative website traffic from January first through today.
example: What is our YTD website traffic?
